title: One turn of a 1 m wheel
hook: A wheel 1 metre across rolls once around. Is that 2 m of ground? 4 m? Something else?

knows: what a circle and its width across (diameter) are
doesNotKnow: that the rim of every circle is a bit more than three times its width across

misconception: The rim is two or four widths long, or the ratio depends on the size of the circle.
objective: The learner can say that one turn of a wheel rolls its rim's length, about 3.14 times its width, the same ratio π for a 1 m and a ½ m wheel.

claims.text: Rolling without slipping lays the whole rim on the ground, so one turn rolls a distance equal to the rim's length.
claims.source: Rolling without slipping: the arc length turned equals the distance travelled (s = rθ; one turn θ = 2π gives s = 2πr). Assumes no slipping.

claims.text: One turn of a 1 m wheel rolls 3.14 m: three wheel-widths and 0.14 m over; a quarter turn is 0.79 m, half 1.57 m, three quarters 2.36 m.
One turn of a ½ m wheel rolls 1.57 m, again 3.14 of its own widths.
For every circle the rim is the same 3.14… times the width across; that number is called π (pi), and circumference = π × diameter.
claims.source: Definition of π as the ratio of circumference to diameter, the same for all circles because circles are similar (scaling multiplies both by the same factor). π ≈ 3.14159 (any reference table).

recall.question: A bicycle wheel is 0.7 m across. About how far does it roll in one full turn?
recall.why: One turn rolls the rim: π × 0.7 ≈ 2.2 m, a bit over three widths.
